clue.text: Builds decrepit cars in Spain? Just the opposite

indicators.note: the surface puts the cars inside Spain, signalling one piece goes inside another
tells us to swap the order the clue gives, so Spain goes inside the cars instead

parts.note: old, battered cars are called crates
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether old bangers turn up in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the opposite' reverses the containment 'in' describes: E (Spain) goes inside CRATES, not the crates inside Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To build something is to make or produce it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Caught unfortunately hugging large soprano

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the word for unfortunately wraps round the letter for large

parts.note: alas expresses regret, like unfortunately

explanation.surface: A large soprano, unfortunately, was caught embracing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria Callas was a celebrated Greek-American opera soprano.

clue.text: Car from European country

parts.note: a state is a country

explanation.surface: A car imported from a European country.
explanation.definitionFit: A British estate car is what Americans call a station wagon.

clue.text: Temperature on earth changing and last of life, in conclusion, is endangered

indicators.note: the letters of earth change into a new order
the final letter goes inside the word for conclusion

parts.note: a conclusion is an end

indicators.note: picks the final letter of life

explanation.surface: Climate change on Earth, and finally life itself, is in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges the letters of earth; 'last of' takes the final letter of life, which 'in' places inside the word for conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at risk or under threat of harm or extinction, a synonym.

clue.text: Begin second pastry

parts.note: a tart is a pastry

explanation.surface: Starting on a second pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: To commence something is to set it going, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Rich, that woman's relatives

parts.note: rich food is fatty, so rich gives fat
belonging to that woman, i.e. hers

explanation.surface: A remark about a wealthy woman's family.
explanation.definitionFit: Male parents and forebears are a kind of relative, so the plural fits relatives.

clue.text: Out of one's mind?

parts.note: usually means mad, but read literally it is something no longer in one's memory

explanation.surface: Someone is asked whether they've gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for insanity is read literally: what has slipped out of the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer remembered has literally left a person's memory.

clue.text: Upset by setter's first clues

parts.note: to upset a container is to tip it over

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of setter's

explanation.surface: A solver is upset by the setter's opening clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Hints or pointers, pieces of useful advice, like clues.

clue.text: Looked at assessment and longed to leave quietly

parts.note: an exam is an assessment

indicators.note: the letter for quietly departs from the word

parts.note: to pine is to long for
P is piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: Someone looked at their exam results and quietly wished to slip away.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect something closely is to have looked at it, a synonym.

clue.text: Small baby, on paper, is most cute

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit on top of the paper

parts.note: baby as an adjective means tiny, Scottish wee
an exam paper is a test

explanation.surface: A tiny baby is, on paper, the cutest.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of a word meaning lovely or charming, as cute is.

clue.text: Student scoffed right after that

parts.note: L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates
to scoff is to eat greedily, so scoffed is ate

explanation.surface: A student ate greedily and then did something right afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsequently or afterwards; the phrase and the adverb are interchangeable synonyms.

clue.text: Jumbo perhaps moved ear over tree

indicators.note: the letters of the word ear are shifted into a new order

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
the plane is a tree common in London streets

explanation.surface: Someone's jumbo-sized ear has been shifted over a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' suggests an elephant, whose ears are huge; here it is the jumbo jet.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumbo jet is one example of a fixed-wing aircraft, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Draw bat without black grip

indicators.note: bat appears without one of its letters, so something is removed

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
traction is the grip of a tyre on a surface

explanation.surface: Advice to draw a bat without a black handle grip, like sketching cricket kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A draw is something that pulls in crowds, a lure or appeal.

clue.text: Parliament advice? It's regularly ignored

indicators.note: every other letter of advice and it's is skipped, keeping the alternate ones

explanation.surface: Wry joke: advice given in parliament is routinely ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advice' points at dieting advice, but the definition is the legislative sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Some national legislatures, such as Japan's, are formally called by this name.

clue.text: Runs ballot, taking on board female's opinion

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: absorbing a letter inside the word for ballot

parts.note: an election is a ballot
F is the abbreviation for female; 's is a link

explanation.surface: Someone runs a ballot that takes a woman's view into account.
explanation.definitionFit: A considered thought or view on something, so a synonym for opinion.

clue.text: Neither vessel at sea avoiding current, despite everything

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters are mixed up
the letters for current are left out of the mixed letters

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Neither ship at sea managed to steer clear of the current, whatever happened.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I (current) from NEITHER VESSEL and rearrange what is left ('at sea').
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning all the same or in spite of that, the phrase and adverb are synonyms.

clue.text: Boris Johnson imprisoned by Queen — it altered things

indicators.note: the letters of Queen and it are changed into a new order
the politician is held among the letters of Queen, joining the pool that is rearranged

parts.note: Boris Johnson was an MP, a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson locked up by the Queen, and that changed everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned by' puts the politician inside the royal letters before 'altered' shuffles the lot. Boris Johnson is a former British Prime Minister, used here only as a Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear or kit, one's things, as in pack your equipment.

clue.text: House could be this busy

definitions.meaning: a house with people living in it is lived in
someone busy has their hands full

explanation.definitionFit: A tenanted house is lived in, and a busy person is tied up, both senses.

clue.text: One who designs endless list

indicators.note: drop the final letter of the word

parts.note: an inventory is a list of items

explanation.surface: Someone who designs an endless list.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who devises new machines or processes is the creator of designs.

clue.text: So, Conservative only quietens rebels after one leaves

indicators.note: the letters rebel against their order, so they are rearranged
when a letter leaves, it is taken out of the pool of letters before they are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A political tale: Conservative only silences rebels once one has walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: C + ONLY + QUIETENS, minus I (one), rearranged ('rebels').
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean therefore or as a result, a direct synonym of the connective.

clue.text: Take care of silver in bushy head of hair

indicators.note: silver goes inside the hair word

parts.note: a mane is a thick head of hair
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone tends silver strands in their bushy hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle or run something is to look after it, a synonym.

clue.text: So — losing old lock generates anxiety

indicators.note: So loses one of its letters

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Losing an old lock of hair causes worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental strain or pressure, a direct synonym for anxiety.

clue.text: Drug-taker's ploy — run to the back

indicators.note: the letter for run travels to the end of the word

parts.note: a ploy is a ruse, a trick
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An addict's trick is to run to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes drugs habitually is commonly called this, a slang sense.

clue.text: RAF accepts new rocket?

indicators.note: the letters are made new by rearranging them

explanation.surface: The Royal Air Force takes delivery of a new rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket is one kind of vehicle that travels into space, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Best 1500m runner preserves energy

indicators.note: the runner keeps energy within him

parts.note: Steve Cram was a British 1500m world record holder
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A top middle-distance runner saves energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Steve Cram was a British middle-distance runner of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its finest part, the best.

clue.text: Bittern evidently eating another bird

indicators.note: the clue words contain the answer, as if eating it

explanation.surface: A bittern has apparently eaten another bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea eagle is a bird, other than the bittern named in the clue.

clue.text: Negotiate to bury editor in church

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: the editor goes inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Arranging for an editor to be buried inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To mediate between parties is to step in and negotiate for them.

clue.text: Blackbeard maybe wanting head hacked off

indicators.note: lacking its first letter, the head being the top of a down or start of a word

parts.note: Blackbeard was a famous pirate, so he is an example

explanation.surface: Blackbeard, perhaps, wanting to have someone's head chopped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacked off' seems to describe beheading but is British slang for annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacked off is informal British for annoyed or angry, a synonym.

clue.text: Most gloomy shoot — describing Ken Loach film

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so dart goes round the film

parts.note: to shoot off is to dart
Kes (1969) is Ken Loach's film about a boy and his kestrel

explanation.surface: A shoot of a gloomy Ken Loach film.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Loach is a British director known for gritty social dramas.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of a word meaning dim or sombre, matching 'most gloomy'.

clue.text: After half a day, openers can be animals

indicators.note: the openers come after the half-day

parts.note: the first half of the word Monday
keys are things that open locks

explanation.surface: After a half-day off, those first to open up can act like animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Primates such as macaques are animals, the plural noun matching.
